project_announced_description: This Rural Development Investment will be used to purchase and install a 66 kilowatts (kW) roof mounted solar array for Tuckahoe Turf Farms in Hammonton, Atlantic County, New Jersey. This project, when completed, will generate 85,353 kilowatt hours (kWh) with an annual savings of $14,429.

funding_code: (COMB LOAN & GRANT) WATER ONLY
naics_industry_sector: Utilities
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will provide additional funding for the extension of the water distribution system along Fidler Hill Road, extension of the boroughs water system within the Municipal airport complex to provide looping of an existing dead-end water main, and upgrades of various components of the Boroughs water supply and treatment plant. The scope of work has expanded with a resulting increase in construction costs that were approved in the original PER Report , dated July 2016. Additional work to be added to the project include providing automatic valving and controls for the pressure filters, providing temporary pressure filters during construction, the addition of a substantial amount of storm drainage improvements at the existing water plant site, and including air relief valves on the water main extension portion of the project. This additional list of work items also increased the basic engineering design fees and resident inspection services. The New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection also decided that certain components of the water plant improvements will require permitting from their office, which was not originally anticipated in the original project scope. Because the Woodbine water plant exists within the boundaries of the Pinelands National Reserve, the NJ-Pinelands Commission is also requiring that the adjacent Borough owned site next to the existing water plant be incorporated into the plant lot which dictates the need for additional surveying, mapping, and permitting services from the design engineer.

naics_industry_sector: Utilities
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to provide additional funding to replace individual septic systems in the Fortescue and Gandys Beach neighborhoods of the Township of Downe, N.J. which are prone to frequent flooding due to their location along the Delaware Bay area. The current conditions are a health and sanitary problem due to sewage overflows of septic tanks from flooding and the resulting contamination of the Delaware Bay. A new sanitary sewer system is to be installed in the Fortescue and Gandys Beach areas consisting of force mains, a sewer pumping station, and packaged wastewater treatment plant to discharge the treated effluent in accordance with permit limits of the New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection. The piping installed will be primarily located in existing roadways to minimize any environmental impacts, and the packaged treatment plant will be located outside and above the limits of the existing floodplain.

funding_code: (WWA PROGRAM AREA) SOLID WASTE GRANT
naics_industry_sector: Utilities
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used for a Solid Waste Management Grant at Rowan University to develop and provide highly specialized hands on technical assistance, onsite training, and education to landfill operators, solid waste commission members and residents of rural communities within rural counties of New Jersey. Recipients will learn to identify potential threats and properly respond to and handle landfill fires. This proposal focuses on proactive waste management through infrared thermography for landfill monitoring and fire warning and aims to help the participants understand the health, economic and environmental effects of landfill fires, and their impact on water, air and soil. This program also educates residents on waste reduction, recycling and composting in their own community through classroom instruction, individual community assistance, in person hands on field work, distribution of informational brochures and a designated webpage. The developed thermal monitoring technique will also be applied to landfills in other parts of New Jersey and has the potential to be used across the country.

funding_code: (COMB LOAN & GRANT) WATER ONLY
naics_industry_sector: Utilities
project_announced_description: The Rural Development investment will be used to install a new water line between Lake Rutherford, N.J. and the water treatment facility located near the Colesville, N.J. reservoir. During heavy rain events, water coming from Lake Rutherford picks up heavy sediment, saturating Colesville reservoir and sends untreatable water into the treatment facility in the Borough of Sussex, N.J. The facility must be shut down until the event subsides. New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection has ordered this issue must be remediated because of health risks associated with this turbid water with an administrative consent order. Installation of a new water line between Lake Rutherford and the treatment facility will address the turbidity issue and the water treatment facility will not incur service shut downs.

naics_industry_sector: Agriculture, Forestry, Fishing and Hunting
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to improve access to preserved farmland through advocacy and acquisition of affordable long-term leases to farmers in New Jersey. The Sustainable Agricultural Enterprise (SAgE) Project will provide more affordable farmland within the State of New Jersey, and increase utilization of government-owned, deed-restricted farmland. The project will enable pilot grows for producers undertaking new crops and value added production. The project will also provide producers with on-farm technical assistance by hiring a Farm Project Manager to assist the ag producers with their projects.

funding_code: RBCS DEVELOPMENT GRANT
naics_industry_sector: Public Administration
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to conduct a feasibility study for the development of a public market facility that will serve businesses and residents of Hackettstown and its surrounding communities. This project will provide new businesses looking to locate in Hackettstown with vendor space, and provide Hackettstowns existing businesses with an increased customer base. The project will give consumers the opportunity to dine, congregate, network, and shop thereby increasing the foot traffic in Hackettstowns Downtown business district. The project will promote locally produced foods by giving farmers a platform to market and distribute their products to consumers of the rural community.
